title: Microbench notelet: small quant runs & prompt seeds
content:
Goal: quick, messy notes for few-shot microbench and quant experiments. Keep ephemeral.

Top-line findings so far (quick):
- NF4 PTQ on 7B gives ~1.8x token throughput improvement vs fp16 at batch=1 on A100, loss ~+0.6 ppl for story prompts (small sample).
- GPTQ-ish 4-bit (per-channel) seems better on longer contexts (seq=1024) vs row-wise; NV memory savings noticeable, kernel warmup cost visible.
- KV cache prefix reuse: for repeated system prompts + shared prefix, observed 6-9% end-to-end latency reduction when cache hits are warm. Need more runs.

Loose todo (next 48h):
- [ ] Re-run nf4 vs gptq 7B with seeds 7, 23, 59 (three runs) for two prompt families (roleplay, summarization). Save logs to bench-run-20260313.
- [ ] Add latency traces (tiny) with --trace-kernel and collect p50/p95 for token generation step (not total).
- [ ] Try static vs dynamic KV caching: script bench/cache_experiments.py (flag --static-prefix-size).
- [ ] Perf ticket to infra: request smaller CUDA persistent pool for short-lived containers (INF-xxxx).

Prompt sets (quick copy):
- roleplay-short: 
  "You are an expert editor. Improve the clarity: 
  
  INPUT: {text}
  OUTPUT:"
- summarization-long: 
  "Condense the passage into 3 bullets, keep facts, remove filler. PASSAGE: {text}
  SUMMARY:"
- retrieval-qa seed example: 
  "You are a search assistant. Given snippets, pick the most relevant sentence and explain why in one line. SNIPPETS: {snips}
  ANSWER:"

Experiment commands (local bench machine):
- baseline fp16 run: python bench/run_microbench.py --model redwood/7B --dtype fp16 --batch 1 --seq 512 --out ./runs/fp16_s512_b1.log
- nf4 ptq: python bench/run_microbench.py --model redwood/7B --dtype nf4 --ptq yes --batch 1 --seq 512 --out ./runs/nf4_s512_b1.log
- gptq-ish: python bench/run_microbench.py --model redwood/7B --dtype int4 --gptq yes --batch 1 --seq 1024 --out ./runs/gptq_s1024_b1.log

Quick metrics to capture in run summary (one-line):
- tokens/sec (inference step), p50_latency_token_ms, p95_latency_token_ms, perplexity / ppl (on small eval set), MRR@10 (if retrieval).

Notes-to-self about quantization artifacts:
- watch for odd tokenization artifacts: sometimes nf4 conversion introduced increased repetition on early tokens in interactive prompts. Could be KL drift in distribution.
- layerwise outliers: layer 12 and 18 show larger quantization error (run per-layer MSE script). Consider per-layer bit allocation or outlier-aware folding.

Unresolved questions / hypotheses:
- H1: For short chats (<128 tokens), nf4 wins on latency + cost, but for longer sequences (>512) GPTQ 4-bit with better outlier handling might maintain quality — test.
- H2: KV cache warm-start benefits are function of prefix length distribution; need to synthesize synthetic prefixes and measure cache hit rate impact on end-to-end.

Notes on eval set (tiny):
- 40 prompts: 10 roleplay-short, 15 summarization-long, 15 retrieval-qa. Keep random seed fixed (seed=42). Small eval but fast.
- Save eval artifacts: runs/eval-seed42/ (log, generated outputs, token-level latencies).

Housekeeping / where to stash outputs:
- small run artifacts -> s3://redwood-playground/microbench/2026-03/ (ask Jordan for temporary write creds)
- larger runs -> bench-nfs1:/mnt/bench-archive/quarter1/2026

Slack notes to self: ping @jordan if run > 3h; mention issues in #infra-bench.

Rough next-day plan:
- morning: re-run nf4/gptq seeds; collect traces; quick summary in PR description for benchmark PR.
- afternoon: try smaller batch sizes (0.5? sim) and one warmup experiment (5 warm tokens) to see kernel warmup shape.

Random micro-things I noticed:
- small model conversion script conv/quantize_v2.py prints a warning about "outlier clamp" defaulting to 2.5 — try lowering to 2.0 to see quality tradeoff.
- GPU mem fragmentation: restart container between runs if mem footprint drifts +2%.

If time: run a tiny AB test where prompts include an extra system instruction and measure change in MRR and repetition.

End of notelet. Keep ephemeral.

-- Anika
